h: Dolphins, Fittie and the beach front
p: Torry is one of the most interesting corners of Aberdeen to bounce in, because some of the city's best free sights are right on its doorstep. Once the trampolining's done, head up to the Torry Battery, the old gun battery on the headland overlooking the harbour mouth. It's one of the best spots in the city to look out for the bottlenose dolphins that are regularly seen feeding where the River Dee meets the sea. Bring patience and a warm coat, because the wind off the North Sea doesn't mess about.

Just across the water, Footdee, known locally as Fittie, is a quirky little fishing village of tiny cottages and colourful sheds tucked in at the end of the beach. It's a lovely place for a quiet wander and some photos. From there, the long sandy beach and Beach Boulevard stretch north, with Codona's amusement park, arcades and rides for anyone who isn't bounced out just yet.

If you'd rather something calmer, Duthie Park on the banks of the Dee has the David Welch Winter Gardens, a series of glasshouses packed with cacti, tropical plants and a fernery, and it's free to visit. Aberdeen Maritime Museum on Shiprow tells the story of the city's relationship with the sea, from shipbuilding to the North Sea oil industry, and has great views over the harbour. A tip for planning: AirHop sessions can be a hot ticket on wet weekends and during school holidays, so book ahead and keep the rest of the day flexible depending on the weather. Aberdeen has a habit of throwing four seasons at you in one afternoon, so layers are your friend.
